newsitem.title: CANADA: BC Sugar rises on new takeover deal.
newsitem.headline: BC Sugar rises on new takeover deal.

text.p: Shares in BC Sugar Refinery Ltd jumped on Thursday after the company agreed to a C$16.50 a share takeover bid by Onex Corp and Balaclava Enterprises.
The stock was up 1.30 to 16.35 in Toronto, making it one of the biggest gainers. Turnover was 17,200 shares.
Vancouver businessman Stuart Belkin, who controls Balaclava, and financier Jim Pattison have been competing for months to take over the sugar refinery.

BC Sugar previously recommended an offer from Pattison's Great Pacific Acquisition Inc of C$15 a share in cash or a class A non-voting share in Great Pacific. Pattison intends to tender his 28 percent stake in BC Sugar to the new bid.

Analysts were surprised by the latest twist but said the new C$415 million deal was virtually certain to end the saga. The C$1.50 a share increase in price and Pattison's decision to tender to the offer will assure Balaclava and Onex victory, they said.
"It has come to and end now. They will get control," said Goepel Shields analyst Carl Hoyt.
Balaclava did not say why it enlisted Onex to join the offer but analysts speculated it did not have the financial resources to make the higher offer on its own.
Balaclava and Onex officials were not available for comment. Onex will own 75 percent of the company formed to make the acquisition and Balaclava the rest.

Balaclava was obliged to offer a significant premium to Pattison's last offer, especially because BC Sugar must now pay a C$5 million kill fee, Hoyt said. "It had to be at least C$1 (more) or else it would just seem they were nickle-and-diming," he said.

Nick Desmarais, a top Pattison adviser, declined to say why his group dropped out of the bidding or if it felt the C$16.50 price tag was justified. He said Pattison was caught off guard by the joint Onex-Balaclava bid.
"We are satisfied with the price. We're going to tender our shares and we wish them well," said Desmarais, who said Pattison harbored no bitterness after the protracted battle.
